text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe remains cautious on planned cuts in taxes and labour charges.
-- Head of supervisory board of Casino supermarkets says in an interview retail sector needs to internationalise, adds Casino needs to build French group able to compete with Carrefour.
-- Insurer GAN expected to post losses around five billion francs for 1996, expects a 20-billion-franc state recapitalisation.
-- Paribas sells its 3.5 percent stake in Havas for one billion francs.
-- Dassault Aviation posts a 917-million-franc profit for 1996, partly due to capital gains.
-- French pharmaceutical industry as a whole registered flat growth in the first quarter due to cuts in prescriptions, except for laboratories which put out new products.
-- IMF sees phase three of European Monetary Union starting on schedule.
-- Thirty six percent of the French remain undecided over which candidate they will vote for, a Figaro-Sofres poll shows, sees the centre-right ruling coalition winning the election with 329 seats.

-- Usinor chairman Francis Mer says in an interview he expects an "excellent" year 1998, considers setting up operations in India, China and eventually in Latin America. Usinor is seen as the most likely candidate to win bid for privatisation of Spanish steelmaker CSI.

-- Member of Bank of France Monetary Policy council Jean-Pierre Gerard says in an interview a late arrival of southern European countries in the European Monetary union would create imbalances, and would favour a delay in launching the euro if the convergence criteria were not met.

-- Group of Seven finance ministers and central bankers meeting in Washington suggested on Sunday the dollar's rise has gone far enough and that they were willing to cooperate to keep world foreign exchange rates stable.
